card.title: FB-MOTE: light-adaptive neural recording
card.imageAlt: FB-MOTE characterization on an illuminated probe station under a microscope

title: A 43 μm × 269 μm Light-Adaptive Optoelectronic Autonomous Microsystem for Neural Recording
venue: IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Circuits and Systems
summary: A 43 μm × 269 μm neural recording microsystem that harvests light through forward-biased CMOS junctions, adapts its bandwidth to available power, and transmits neural signals as optical pulses.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: FB-MOTE is a light-powered neural recording microsystem that collects photogenerated carriers through the intrinsic junctions of its CMOS bulk. The harvested energy supports amplification, encoding and optical communication in a compact footprint.

Fabricated in 180 nm CMOS, each recording unit measures approximately 43 μm × 269 μm. Its bandwidth grows with available optical power while the integrated input-referred noise remains relatively stable.
bullets: Forward-bulk energy harvesting with AlGaAs optical telemetry.

images.alt: CMOS test die with a 3 by 26 FB-MOTE array, a single unit pad map, and its annotated circuit layout
images.caption: The 180 nm CMOS test die, unit pad map and circuit layout.

sections.heading: Forward-bulk optical powering
paragraphs: Forward bias allows the CMOS silicon junctions to act as photovoltaic sources and lowers transistor threshold voltages. Red illumination at 637 nm powers both the CMOS bulk and a dual-function AlGaAs photovoltaic/light-emitting diode (PVLED). The PVLED supplies the charge pump and emits the encoded optical pulses at approximately 835 nm.

An inverter-based amplifier uses switched-capacitor feedback to reduce sensitivity to light-induced leakage. Most additional current is directed to amplification, while proportional-to-absolute-temperature biasing keeps the other circuit blocks comparatively stable. Complementary pulse pairs encode the neural signal using pulse position modulation (PPM).

images.alt: FB-MOTE circuit block diagram showing silicon photovoltaic harvesting, the amplifier and encoder, and the PVLED-powered charge pump and LED driver
images.caption: Signal chain and power domains: the CMOS bulk supplies the recording circuits, while the PVLED powers the charge pump for optical transmission.

sections.heading: Power-adaptive neural recording
paragraphs: In probe-based optical measurements, increasing irradiance expands the recording bandwidth while integrated input-referred noise stays around 14–15 μV RMS. At approximately 1100 μW/mm², the bandwidth reaches about 12 kHz, improving reconstruction of higher-frequency action-potential features.

A pre-recorded neural waveform containing local field potentials and action potentials was applied to the chip inputs and recovered from its optical output. Recording remains clear near 1200 μW/mm²; increasing illumination to 1250 μW/mm² produces distortion and higher noise. These limits describe the probe-based test configuration.

images.alt: Optical characterization plots of normalized gain, pulse encoding, bandwidth, oscillator period, supply voltage and noise versus irradiance
images.caption: Measured circuit response under optical powering, including bandwidth, timing, supply voltage and input-referred noise.

images.alt: Ground-truth neural waveform and four decoded FB-MOTE recordings at illumination levels from 100 to 1250 microwatts per square millimetre
images.caption: Reconstruction of an injected, pre-recorded neural waveform at 100, 1100, 1200 and 1250 μW/mm². Shaded intervals highlight action potentials.

sections.heading: Biological validation
paragraphs: Functional tests used optically powered, wire-bonded chips connected to external platinum microelectrodes. In phosphate-buffered saline, the decoded output reproduced an applied electric field carrying a pre-recorded neural waveform.

Acute recordings from an earthworm ventral nerve were compared with a simultaneously connected LT1793-based control amplifier. After compensating for the fixed decoding latency, the FB-MOTE output agreed with the control in timing and waveform morphology.
bullets: Average input-referred noise in open air: 14.51 μV RMS.
In the acute earthworm experiment: 15.83 μV RMS.

images.alt: Saline recording setup and traces, acute earthworm nerve recording with a control amplifier, and noise measurements across optical illumination levels
images.caption: Optically powered saline and acute earthworm recordings using external Pt electrodes, with corresponding waveform comparisons and noise measurements.

sections.heading: Optical decoding
paragraphs: The external receiver detects optical pulses and processes them in 100 ms batches. Histogram compression and Otsu thresholding identify pulses; timing statistics recover the reference-pulse grid. The complementary encoding intervals are then combined to reconstruct the neural voltage.

A two-node demonstration separates channels by pulse amplitude when the contrast is sufficient. For similar amplitudes, reference timing and a lightweight Viterbi path help recover the channel assignments. The examples use a sine wave on one node and a neural signal on the other.

images.alt: Detected reference and encoding pulses, two pseudo-chopping traces and the reconstructed neural waveform
images.caption: Reference and encoding pulse timing, intermediate pseudo-chopping traces, and the reconstructed neural signal.

images.alt: Two-node optical decoding with a sine-wave channel and a neural-signal channel, comparing distinct and similar pulse amplitudes
images.caption: Two-node decoding with distinct pulse amplitudes and with similar amplitudes. Each node carries a different input waveform.

sections.heading: Light-aware modeling
paragraphs: Optical and electrical powering produce measurable differences in oscillator timing. Adding empirical photocurrent sources to the extracted circuit model captures the optical measurements more closely. Minority-carrier diffusion is proposed as an explanation; dedicated test structures would be needed to validate that mechanism.

The paper also reports wire-bonding damage to metal-insulator-metal capacitors and an earlier optical cutoff near 780 μW/mm² in wire-bonded samples. Probe-based performance and wire-bonded biological tests therefore describe different integration conditions.

images.alt: Measured oscillator periods and bandwidths under electrical and optical powering, compared with extracted circuit simulations and an empirical photocurrent model
images.caption: Electrical and optical measurements compared with extracted simulations. Empirical photocurrent sources improve the timing agreement under illumination.
